{"metadata":{"description":"Zero-config Exa web search provider for DeepSeek Harness (dsh): keyless anonymous MCP fallback (mcp.exa.ai/mcp) + keyed REST path, with a configurable providerId switch.","id":"gh:1333810190","install_available":true,"language":"JavaScript","name":"dsh-web-search-exa","slug":"TonyDua/dsh-web-search-exa","topics":["cordis","deepseek","deepseek-harness","dsh","dsh-plugin","exa","mcp","web-search"]},"paragraphs":[{"id":"p1s1","text":"Zero-config Exa web search provider for DeepSeek Harness (dsh): keyless anonymous MCP fallback (mcp."},{"id":"p1s2","text":"exa.ai/mcp) + keyed REST path, with a configurable providerId switch."},{"id":"p2s1","text":"# @tonydua/dsh-web-search-exa"},{"id":"p3s1","text":"**English** | 简体中文"},{"id":"p4s1","text":"Adds Exa web search to DeepSeek Harness (dsh), the anonymous no-key variant."},{"id":"p5s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p6s1","text":"Restart `dsh web` and it works. No API key, no config edits, no provider to select."},{"id":"p7s1","text":"Background, for reference only:"},{"id":"p8s1","text":"- **Exa** is a search API. It retrieves pages by keyword or by meaning and returns citable sources w"},{"id":"p8s2","text":"ith excerpts. It does not generate answers. Exa offers a REST API and also runs an unauthenticated p"},{"id":"p8s3","text":"ublic MCP server.
- **The official `dsh-web-search-exa`** is dsh's Exa search provider. It uses Exa'"},{"id":"p8s4","text":"s REST API and is only useful once you configure an API key.
- **This package is a modified copy of "},{"id":"p8s5","text":"the official one.** The REST path works the same. What we added is a keyless channel: with no key it"},{"id":"p8s6","text":" uses Exa's public MCP server, and with a key it still uses REST. The anonymous approach follows the"},{"id":"p8s7","text":" oh-my-pi project, see Acknowledgements."},{"id":"p9s1","text":"You can ignore all of this by default. Read Selecting a provider only if you also run the official p"},{"id":"p9s2","text":"ackage, or if dsh reports an ambiguous provider."},{"id":"p10s1","text":"Built with deepseek-v4-flash inside DeepSeek Harness (dsh). The 0.2.3 live-config work was done with"},{"id":"p10s2","text":"seek-v4-flash inside DeepSeek Harness (dsh). The 0.2.3 live-config work was done with GLM-5.3-flash."},{"id":"p11s1","text":"## Features"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"- Works without a key. Searches go through Exa's public MCP server (`mcp.exa.ai/mcp`) and carry no c"},{"id":"p12s2","text":"redentials.
- Returns structured results on that keyless path. It calls `web_search_advanced_exa`, w"},{"id":"p12s3","text":"hose output is JSON in the REST field vocabulary, so sources carry real highlight snippets without t"},{"id":"p12s4","text":"ext parsing.
- Upgrades itself when you add a key. Setting `EXA_API_KEY` switches to Exa's `POST /se"},{"id":"p12s5","text":"arch` REST API for higher limits, with no behavior change.
- Drop-in. It registers into the dsh `ctx"},{"id":"p12s6","text":".web` seam; the model-facing `web_search` and `web_fetch` tools, their prompt sections, and the resu"},{"id":"p12s7","text":"lt cards all stay as they are.
- Works out of the box. With no official package installed there is n"},{"id":"p12s8","text":"o provider to select.
- Backs off when it fails. After repeated failures on the anonymous channel th"},{"id":"p12s9","text":"e plugin marks itself unavailable so dsh can pick another provider, instead of failing every search."},{"id":"p12s10","text":" See What happens when a search fails."},{"id":"p13s1","text":"## How it works"},{"id":"p14s1","text":"| Condition | Path | Endpoint |"},{"id":"p15s1","text":"| `apiKey` / `EXA_API_KEY` configured | REST `POST /search` with `Authorization: Bearer` | `https://"},{"id":"p15s2","text":"api.exa.ai/search` (configurable via `baseURL`) |
| No key configured | Anonymous MCP `tools/call we"},{"id":"p15s3","text":"b_search_advanced_exa` (JSON-RPC 2.0, no credentials) | `https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp?tools=…` (configurab"},{"id":"p15s4","text":"rch_advanced_exa` (JSON-RPC 2.0, no credentials) | `https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp?tools=…` (configurable) |"},{"id":"p16s1","text":"The anonymous MCP path sends no credentials; attribution rides the `x-exa-source: dsh-anything` head"},{"id":"p16s2","text":"er. Results are normalized to the seam's `WebSearchSource` shape (`url`, `title`, `snippet`, `publis"},{"id":"p16s3","text":"hedAt`), and the seam enforces `maxResults` on the way back."},{"id":"p17s1","text":"The anonymous path calls `web_search_advanced_exa` by default. Its text content is a sanitized JSON "},{"id":"p17s2","text":"search response whose entries use the same field names as the REST API, so a result maps to a source"},{"id":"p17s3","text":" directly and no `Title:`-section text parsing is involved. Two consequences worth knowing:"},{"id":"p18s1","text":"- **The structured tool is only served when the URL carries `?tools=…`.** The bare endpoint answers "},{"id":"p18s2","text":"`MCP error -32602: Tool web_search_advanced_exa not found`, which is why that query is part of the d"},{"id":"p18s3","text":"efault `mcpURL` and why the plugin splices it into any `mcpURL` that lacks it.
- **It returns whole-"},{"id":"p18s4","text":"page text for every hit, and we ask for highlights separately.** Without `enableHighlights` the endp"},{"id":"p18s5","text":"oint returns text-only entries, every result would lack a snippet, and the search would come back em"},{"id":"p18s6","text":"pty. The full text is discarded: a snippet is always a real highlight sentence, never generated and "},{"id":"p18s7","text":"never lifted from the page body."},{"id":"p19s1","text":"`searchType` is not forwarded here. The plugin's setting uses the REST vocabulary (`auto`, `keyword`"},{"id":"p19s2","text":", `neural`) while the tool accepts its own (`auto`, `fast`, `instant`), so forwarding it would make "},{"id":"p19s3","text":"a configured `keyword` or `neural` fail argument validation and take the whole anonymous path down. "},{"id":"p19s4","text":"The tool's default is what `auto` asks for anyway."},{"id":"p20s1","text":"Pinning `mcpTool: web_search_exa` restores the older text-blob path, where the same results arrive a"},{"id":"p20s2","text":"s `Title:`-led sections. Use it if Exa changes the structured tool's shape; a body that is not the e"},{"id":"p20s3","text":"xpected JSON already falls back to section parsing on its own."},{"id":"p21s1","text":"[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p22s1","text":"## Version compatibility"},{"id":"p23s1","text":"Every published dsh version from `0.1.2-alpha.2` to `0.2.1-alpha.1` has been tested. Testing means t"},{"id":"p23s2","text":"hree things: installing that version in isolation, typechecking against its own declarations, and in"},{"id":"p23s3","text":"stalling this plugin with npm under strict peer resolution. The last step is the one that fails most"},{"id":"p23s4","text":" easily, because npm's peer rules are stricter than pnpm's. To reproduce: `bash scripts/compat-matri"},{"id":"p23s5","text":"y, because npm's peer rules are stricter than pnpm's. To reproduce: `bash scripts/compat-matrix.sh`."},{"id":"p24s1","text":"| dsh line | Tested | Notes |"},{"id":"p25s1","text":"| `0.1.2-alpha.2` … `0.1.2-alpha.5` | ✅ | the oldest supported baseline |
| `0.1.2-rc.1` | ✅ | |
| `"},{"id":"p25s2","text":"0.1.3-alpha.2` | ✅ | |
| `0.1.5-alpha.1`, `0.1.5-alpha.2` | ✅ | |
| `0.1.5-rc.1`, `0.1.5-rc.2`, `0.1"},{"id":"p25s3","text":".5-rc.3` | ✅ | `0.1.5-rc.2` is also verified end to end: a real `dsh --profile headless` task search"},{"id":"p25s4","text":"ed through the anonymous MCP path with no API key |
| `0.1.6-alpha.1`, `0.1.6-alpha.2` | ✅ | |
| `0."},{"id":"p25s5","text":"1.7-alpha.1` | ✅ | the settings service changed shape, see below |
| `0.2.0-rc.1`, `0.2.0-rc.2` | ✅ "},{"id":"p25s6","text":"| strict npm install beside the host, then a live keyless search |
| `0.2.1-alpha.1` | ✅ | same, and"},{"id":"p25s7","text":" the only version that needs `@deepseek-ai/cordis@4.0.5-alpha.1` |"},{"id":"p26s1","text":"Versions from the `0.2.0-rc.1` line onward are additionally declared, one full version at a time, un"},{"id":"p26s2","text":"der `dsh.compatibility.dshReleases` in `package.json`. That key is catalog metadata: the dsh runtime"},{"id":"p26s3","text":" never reads it, and it does not affect resolution — registries such as DSH STORE require an exact p"},{"id":"p26s4","text":"er-version record, and a peer range is not installable evidence. The declarations cover `0.2.0-rc.1`"},{"id":"p26s5","text":", `0.2.0-rc.2`, and `0.2.1-alpha.1`, all `compatible`."}],"truncated":true}
